executive_summary: This EIC Pathfinder Challenge funds research to make quantum technologies energy-efficient and to benchmark their energy use: each project focuses on one area, full-stack quantum computing, quantum communication or quantum sensing, and must reach TRL 3-4 with prototypes or testbeds that use less energy than classical counterparts (or than state-of-the-art quantum solutions for fault-tolerant computing). Single legal entities (not mid-caps or large companies) or consortia of two, or three or more, entities may apply. The grant is a Research and Innovation Action lump sum at 100% of eligible costs, with up to EUR 4 million per project considered appropriate; the EUR 82 million Challenges budget is shared roughly equally across three Challenges. The deadline is 29 September 2027 at 17:00 Brussels time; the call opens on 27 May 2027.
status_rationale: The Challenge funds research on the energy consumption of quantum computing, communication and sensing hardware, with energy-per-task benchmarks and pre-normative energy accounting (EIC Work Programme 2027, Section II.2.3, pp. 46-50). The energy it addresses is the power drawn by the quantum devices themselves, not the electricity system, and the call names no grid or energy-system application, so no project file is close and it does not touch TenneT's field.
